To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the human EJC interacts with SR proteins to form a megadalton sized mRNP structure that is resistant to nuclease digestion.
the EJC interacts with SR proteins and that these interactions are required for EJC stability.
the EJC interacts with SR proteins to form higher-order mRNP structures that promote mRNA compaction and packaging.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of RNA in the formation of higher-order mRNP complexes.
the molecular mechanism of mRNA splicing, which involves the removal of non-coding intron segments from pre-mRNA transcripts.
the role of the spliceosome in mRNA biogenesis and its regulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EJCs are not merely splicing-related factors that are deposited at the exon-exon junction, they are major components of the spliced mRNP.
our study provides a comprehensive view of the endogenous EJC protein and mRNA interactome in human cells.
our study reveals the existence of a higher order EJC-SR protein complex that plays an important role in mRNA compaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EJC and SR protein networks in the cell form a nexus that is essential for mRNP maturation.
EJC and SR protein interactions are a major contributor to the structure of the spliced mRNP.
endogenous EJC core factors, in addition to their canonical function of splicing and exon junction recognition, are also major components of a large, dynamic, and highly ordered mRNP structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EJC and SR protein complexes are a major structural component of the endogenous mRNP, which may be critical for mRNA export, translation, and/or mRNA stability.
endogenous EJC complexes are not simple, monomeric, and static entities but rather are highly dynamic, multicomponent, megadalton sized structures.
EJCs are not merely static splicing factors but instead are dynamic components of the mRNP interactome.
